sections.title: Front matter

summary.text: Front matter of the 2021 WHO guidance 'Leave no one behind: guidance for planning and implementing catch-up vaccination', including copyright and licensing details, table of contents, acknowledgements, abbreviations, glossary of key terms, and an executive overview. It outlines how continuous catch-up vaccination and special post-disruption catch-up efforts close immunity gaps, strengthen primary health care, and reduce reliance on costly mass campaigns.

sections.title: Principles of catch-up vaccination
Introduction

summary.text: Introduces Section 1 on the core principles of catch-up vaccination, emphasizing that almost all vaccines are safe and effective to administer late when doses are missed and that no eligible individual should be denied vaccination. It highlights integrating catch-up vaccination into routine immunization programmes across all health system touchpoints to reduce missed opportunities for vaccination (MOV) and summarizes the elements of a strong catch-up strategy in Figure 1.

sections.extract: • Everyone should fully benefit from vaccination by receiving recommended vaccines as soon as they are eligible, and those who arrive “late” should not be denied vaccination. • Most vaccines are safe and effective to administer with no upper age limit and while timely vaccination should always be the aim, it is almost always better to vaccinate late than never. There are a small number of vaccines for which upper

sections.title: Establishing a catch-up vaccination policy and schedule

summary.text: Outlines Section 1.1 on establishing a national catch-up vaccination policy and schedule aligned with the national immunization schedule, clarifying eligibility, permissible age ranges, recording of delayed doses, and screening at every health contact. It recommends engaging National Immunization Technical Advisory Groups (NITAGs) and using the WHO recommendations for interrupted or delayed immunization summary tables to guide policy decision-making.

sections.extract: • Every country should have a clear catch-up vaccination policy and catch-up schedule designed in line with the national immunization schedule. The catch-up policy should provide clarity to health workers on: 1) The importance of providing vaccinations for those who have missed one or more doses within the national immunization schedule, 2) How to determine eligibility including permissible age ranges, 3) Correct

sections.title: Ensuring availability of vaccines and supplies for catch-up vaccination

summary.text: Covers the remainder of Section 1.1 (including Box 1 on designing a catch-up schedule and policies for unconfirmed vaccination history) and Section 1.2 on ensuring the availability of vaccines and supplies for catch-up vaccination. It details forecasting additional buffer stock for older cohorts, applying the multi-dose vial policy (MDVP) to manage open-vial wastage, and using electronic stock management tools such as SMT, wVSSM, and eLMIS.

sections.title: Building health worker knowledge and practice

summary.text: Presents Section 1.3 on building health worker knowledge, attitudes, and practices for administering catch-up vaccinations across expanded age groups through training, supportive supervision, and clear job aids. It includes Box 2, an 11-step summary of operational instructions for health workers covering vaccination history review, minimum ages and intervals, co-administration of multiple overdue antigens, recording actual dose numbers, and scheduling follow-up visits.

sections.extract: • The success of any health intervention depends on competent front-line health workers and managers. For catch-up vaccination to be viewed as a priority, health workers’ interpersonal skills, motivations and attitudes need to be addressed in training, supervision, and the feedback they are given. For programmes that historically limited routine immunization to children <1 year, or children <2 years, the expansion

sections.title: Recording and reporting of catch-up vaccination doses

summary.text: Addresses Section 1.4 on recording and reporting catch-up vaccination doses, explaining how restrictive age-grouped tally sheets, registers, and 12-month coverage reporting cycles can inadvertently discourage late vaccination. It provides guidance on redesigning paper registers, tally sheets, and electronic immunization registries (EIRs) to capture delayed doses, discusses denominator challenges in Box 3, and outlines solutions for strengthening home-based records (HBRs) in Box 4.

sections.extract: • A major challenge for identifying eligibility, administering and monitoring catch-up vaccination is lack of reliable written record of vaccination history (i.e. individual home-based records, facility- based paper registers, or EIRs). • Many immunization information systems are not currently designed to record, and report delayed doses. For example, administrative systems typically record vaccinations by yearly

sections.title: Communication and community engagement

summary.text: Covers Section 1.5 on communication and community engagement for ongoing catch-up vaccination, emphasizing targeted reminders and broad media messaging that late vaccination remains safe and effective. It highlights partnering with civil society, faith-based groups, daycares, and schools to reach vulnerable populations, counter misinformation, and encourage caregivers to bring home-based records to every health visit.

sections.extract: • Targeted communications should inform individuals, caregivers, and communities more broadly of the value of vaccination and the importance of being vaccinated in a timely manner. • Communication with caregivers and individuals through phone calls, emails, and SMS text message reminders, as well as broader messaging through television, radio, social media, posters, etc. should aim to increase awareness that missing

sections.title: Strategies for catch-up vaccination

summary.text: Details Section 1.6 on operational strategies for continuous catch-up vaccination, including newborn and defaulter tracking in routine immunization, integrating 'screen and vaccinate' or referral workflows across broader health services to reduce missed opportunities for vaccination (MOV), and implementing school-based vaccination checks at educational enrollment or during sessions.

sections.extract: Routine immunization services throughout the year • The practice of catch-up vaccination should be integrated into routine immunization service delivery on a continuous basis. Every immunization contact, whether fixed or outreach (including school-based), should be used as an opportunity to review an individual’s vaccination status and catch-up any antigens that have been missed before that visit. • Every health

sections.title: Special catch-up vaccination efforts following an interruption of services

summary.text: Introduces Section 2 on special catch-up vaccination efforts following an interruption of immunization services caused by emergencies, disasters, or vaccine shortages. It stresses integrating ongoing catch-up into routine services as soon as delivery resumes while planning large-scale, intensified efforts and cohort tracking when prolonged disruptions create substantial immunity gaps.

sections.extract: services • Immunization is an essential health service that should continue without interruption to the maximum extent possible under all circumstances. However, in exceptional emergency or disaster situations there may be an interruption or significant drop in routine immunization services, delay or temporary suspension of mass vaccination campaigns, and/or prolonged vaccine shortages, leading to an accumulation of

sections.title: Policy and advocacy

summary.text: Outlines Section 2.1 on policy and advocacy during and after catastrophic events or health system disruptions, calling for immunization recovery to be embedded within coordinated health system recovery plans. It recommends issuing interim catch-up guidance—such as temporarily lifting upper age limits for cohorts missed during disruptions—in consultation with NITAGs and emergency programmes, and rapidly disseminating updated schedules and job aids to all providers.

sections.extract: • During, or in the aftermath of a catastrophic event, whether it be an outbreak, epidemic or pandemic, natural disaster, acute conflict, or other disruption, health systems are likely to be overburdened.33 Finances and human resources may be limited due to reallocation. Supply chains may be disrupted leading to stock-outs of vaccines and supplies. Surveillance systems may have been stopped or diverted. There may be

sections.title: Managing vaccines and supplies

summary.text: Presents Section 2.2 on managing vaccines and supplies during and after service interruptions, including inventory remapping, temperature and VVM monitoring, forecasting surge stock for missed cohorts, and assessing cold chain capacity. It also covers accepting reduced shelf-life vaccines managed under the 'first expiry, first out' (FEFO) principle and utilizing Controlled Temperature Chain (CTC) or Extended Controlled Temperature Conditions (ECTC) where licensed.

sections.extract: • During an interruption in services, supply chains at local, regional, national, and possibly international levels may be affected. Stock out of key supplies may be a challenge, requiring a remapping of inventory, at all levels, and a coordinated redistribution of supplies once delivery channels are reopened. • The situation can be mitigated by the following actions: o Establish and implement procedures for

sections.title: Monitoring the extent of the interruption

summary.text: Covers Section 2.3 on monitoring the extent of service interruptions by tracking coverage, VPD surveillance, AEFIs, and facility logbooks of individuals with pending doses, alongside Box 5 on estimating target populations for intensified catch-up efforts. It also recommends rapid coverage assessments, risk triangulation, and interim recording practices on home-based records and registers when formal information systems lack fields for delayed doses.

sections.extract: • It is important to monitor the situation as closely as possible throughout the period of disruption and track individuals or cohorts missing vaccination as best as possible to inform catch-up strategies. This can be done by: o Continuing to monitor vaccination coverage, VPD surveillance, AEFIs, and vaccine safety concerns in order to identify gaps, inequalities and vulnerable groups and communities. o Maintaining

sections.title: Communication and community engagement

summary.text: Addresses Section 2.4 on communication and community engagement following service disruptions to rebuild public trust, counter rumours through media and digital listening, and conduct formative research on barriers to immunization. It emphasizes informing communities that individuals remain eligible for missed doses, that late vaccines are safe and effective, and where and when services are operating with safety precautions.

sections.extract: • Even if routine immunization services have continued at reduced capacity or once they resume, demand and accessibility may remain low and intermittent interruptions may continue to occur for some time. • Engagement with communities (including local civil society, non-governmental and faith-based organizations, professional associations, etc.) to help design and implement tailored and targeted communication

sections.title: Strategies for catch-up vaccination after an interruption of services

summary.text: Details Section 2.5 on selecting and combining strategies for catch-up vaccination after prolonged service interruptions, including intensified routine outreach, Periodic Intensification of Routine Immunization (PIRI), and supplementary immunization activities (SIAs). It provides decision-making frameworks in Boxes 6 and 7 for epidemiological VPD risk assessment, vaccine delivery amenability, contextual constraints, and infection prevention and control (IPC) measures.

sections.extract: • Offering catch-up vaccination on an ongoing basis through the routine immunization system is the least resource intensive and most sustainable strategy for ensuring individuals are able to receive the vaccines they are due, especially if the service interruption is relatively short. • If immunization services have been impacted for a prolonged period of time, additional strategies to accelerate catch-up

sections.title: Designing Catch-up Vaccination Schedules

summary.text: Presents Annex 1 on designing national, antigen-specific, and population-specific catch-up vaccination schedules with NITAG involvement, linking to country schedule examples. It includes Table A1.1 illustrating a tetanus-toxoid-containing vaccine (TTCV) catch-up schedule and Table A1.2 summarizing WHO recommendations for interrupted or delayed routine immunization across antigens.

sections.extract: Every country should have a catch-up vaccination schedule designed in line with the national immunization schedule, that adhere to any upper or lower age requirements as determined by the national immunization policy. NITAGs should be involved in the process of developing a catch-up vaccination schedule at the earliest opportunity. Catch-up vaccination schedules can be designed in a variety of ways and, as

sections.title: Minimum Intervals between Doses in a Vaccine Series

summary.text: Presents Annex 2 on minimum ages at first dose and minimum permissible intervals between doses in a multi-dose vaccine series to ensure an adequate immune response. It provides a reference table of minimum ages, inter-dose intervals, and age-specific clinical comments for BCG, Hepatitis B, DTP/Td, Polio, Hib, Rotavirus, PCV, MR/MMR, and HPV.

sections.extract: For vaccines requiring multiple doses, the minimum interval is the shortest amount of time permissible between doses in order to provide an adequate immune response. If the interval between the doses is shorter than the minimum interval, the second dose received may not be effective. sections.title: Sample job aids for catch-up vaccination

summary.text: Presents Annex 3 with illustrative sample job aids and links to digital catch-up schedule calculators (such as Australia's NICC, Catchup Ghana, and the US CDC Childhood Vaccine Assessment Tool) to help health workers determine catch-up eligibility and co-administration.

sections.title: Catch-up vaccination worksheet for determining eligibility

summary.text: Presents Annex 4 (an adaptable clinical worksheet for assessing an individual's vaccination history, doses due now, and future catch-up appointments to share with caregivers) and Annex 5 (two example routine childhood vaccination tally sheets designed to record catch-up doses without restrictive upper age limits).

sections.extract: Worksheets like this can be a useful tool to help health workers assess which doses an individual is eligible for at the time of a visit, and when subsequent doses will be needed (to communicate this to the caregiver or individual). sections.title: Periodic Intensification of Routine Immunization: An Overview

summary.text: Presents Annex 6, an overview developed by the ad-hoc workgroup on Periodic Intensification of Routine Immunization (PIRI) describing time-limited, intermittent activities such as Child Health Days and Vaccination Weeks where doses are screened and recorded as routine immunizations. It includes Tables A6.1–A6.3 detailing PIRI goals, a feature comparison against SIAs and routine immunization, and potential PIRI designs tailored to country coverage settings.

sections.title: Actions to enhance acceptance and demand for vaccination

summary.text: Presents Annex 7 on actions to enhance acceptance and demand for vaccination, outlining key communication messages during and after service disruptions, collaboration with local civil society and community leaders, and rumour management. It also covers behavioural and social data collection, health worker training in interpersonal communication, and service quality improvements that foster positive vaccination experiences.

sections.extract: KEY POINTS • Vaccination uptake is affected by both individual, social and practical factors. A circle divided into five coloured segments around a central circle labelled 'Catch-up vaccination policy and schedule'. The segments, clockwise from the top right, are: vaccines and supplies for catch-up vaccination; health worker knowledge and practice; recording and reporting practices, information systems and tools; communications and community engagement to build support; and strategies for catch-up vaccination.

The same figure is also placed on the page as a raster image (img-p011-1).

A table headed 'Minimum interval from the most recent dose administered'. Rows give the age-appropriate vaccine: 1-4 years, DTwP, DTaP or DT; 4-7 years, DTwP, DTaP, Td or DT; over 7 years, Td or TdaP. Columns give the dose, with the same interval for all three rows: 1st dose as early as possible; 2nd dose at least 4 weeks after the 1st; 3rd dose at least 6 months after the 2nd; 4th dose at least 1 year after the 3rd; 5th dose at least 1 year after the 4th.
narratives.fr: Tableau intitulé « Intervalle minimal depuis la dernière dose administrée ». Les lignes indiquent le vaccin adapté à l'âge : 1 à 4 ans, DTCc, DTCa ou DT ; 4 à 7 ans, DTCc, DTCa, Td ou DT ; plus de 7 ans, Td ou dTca. Les colonnes indiquent la dose, avec le même intervalle pour les trois lignes : 1re dose dès que possible ; 2e dose au moins 4 semaines après la 1re ; 3e dose au moins 6 mois après la 2e ; 4e dose au moins 1 an après la 3e ; 5e dose au moins 1 an après la 4e.
narratives.es: Tabla titulada «Intervalo mínimo desde la dosis más reciente administrada». Las filas indican la vacuna apropiada según la edad: 1-4 años, DTPc, DTPa o DT; 4-7 años, DTPc, DTPa, Td o DT; mayores de 7 años, Td o Tdap. Las columnas indican la dosis, con el mismo intervalo en las tres filas: 1.ª dosis lo antes posible; 2.ª dosis al menos 4 semanas después de la 1.ª; 3.ª dosis al menos 6 meses después de la 2.ª; 4.ª dosis al menos 1 año después de la 3.ª; 5.ª dosis al menos 1 año después de la 4.ª.
narratives.ar: جدول بعنوان «الحد الأدنى للفاصل الزمني منذ آخر جرعة مُعطاة». تعرض الصفوف اللقاح المناسب للعمر: 1–4 سنوات، DTwP أو DTaP أو DT؛ 4–7 سنوات، DTwP أو DTaP أو Td أو DT؛ أكثر من 7 سنوات، Td أو TdaP. وتعرض الأعمدة الجرعة، مع الفاصل الزمني نفسه للصفوف الثلاثة جميعها: الجرعة الأولى في أقرب وقت ممكن؛ الجرعة الثانية بعد 4 أسابيع على الأقل من الأولى؛ الجرعة الثالثة بعد 6 أشهر على الأقل من الثانية؛ الجرعة الرابعة بعد سنة واحدة على الأقل من الثالثة؛ الجرعة الخامسة بعد سنة واحدة على الأقل من الرابعة.
narratives.ru: Таблица «Минимальный интервал после последней введенной дозы». В строках указаны вакцины в соответствии с возрастом: 1–4 года — АКДС с цельноклеточным коклюшным компонентом (DTwP), бесклеточная АКДС (DTaP) или АДС (DT); 4–7 лет — DTwP, DTaP, АДС-М (Td) или DT; старше 7 лет — Td или АДС-М с бесклеточным коклюшным компонентом (TdaP). В столбцах указаны дозы с одинаковым интервалом для всех трех строк: 1-я доза — как можно раньше; 2-я доза — не менее чем через 4 недели после 1-й; 3-я доза — не менее чем через 6 месяцев после 2-й; 4-я доза — не менее чем через 1 год после 3-й; 5-я доза — не менее чем через 1 год после 4-й.

narratives.en: An 'Instructions' panel of three steps for the health worker. Step 1: praise the parent or caregiver for bringing the child, and find out from the immunization record or caregiver how old the child is today and which vaccines the child has already received. Step 2: use the chart to the right to decide what to give; the child should already have received all vaccines due up to their current age, and if doses are missing it is not too late; administer the vaccines for which the child is eligible, respecting the necessary spacing. Step 3: remind the caregiver when to bring the child back for subsequent doses and emphasise the importance of completing the series. Cartoon drawings of a standing girl and a seated baby decorate the panel.
narratives.fr: Panneau « Instructions » en trois étapes destiné à l'agent de santé. Étape 1 : féliciter le parent ou la personne en charge d'avoir amené l'enfant, et déterminer à partir du carnet de vaccination ou auprès de l'accompagnant l'âge actuel de l'enfant et les vaccins qu'il a déjà reçus. Étape 2 : utiliser le tableau de droite pour décider quels vaccins administrer ; l'enfant devrait déjà avoir reçu tous les vaccins prévus jusqu'à son âge actuel, et s'il manque des doses il n'est pas trop tard ; administrer les vaccins auxquels l'enfant est éligible en respectant les intervalles requis. Étape 3 : rappeler à l'accompagnant quand ramener l'enfant pour les doses suivantes et souligner l'importance d'achever la série vaccinale. Des illustrations de dessin animé représentant une fillette debout et un bébé assis décorent le panneau.
narratives.es: Panel de «Instrucciones» en tres pasos para el trabajador de salud. Paso 1: felicitar al padre, madre o cuidador por traer al niño, y averiguar mediante el carné de vacunación o el cuidador qué edad tiene hoy el niño y qué vacunas ha recibido ya. Paso 2: utilizar el cuadro de la derecha para decidir qué administrar; el niño ya debería haber recibido todas las vacunas correspondientes hasta su edad actual y, si faltan dosis, aún no es demasiado tarde; administrar las vacunas para las que el niño reúna los requisitos, respetando los intervalos necesarios. Paso 3: recordar al cuidador cuándo debe traer nuevamente al niño para las dosis subsiguientes y recalcar la importancia de completar el esquema. Dibujos animados de una niña de pie y un bebé sentado decoran el panel.
narratives.ar: لوحة «تعليمات» مكوّنة من ثلاث خطوات للعامل الصحي. الخطوة 1: الثناء على الوالد أو مقدّم الرعاية لإحضار الطفل، ومعرفة عمر الطفل اليوم واللقاحات التي تلقاها بالفعل من سجل التطعيم أو من مقدّم الرعاية. الخطوة 2: استخدام المخطط الموجود على اليمين لتحديد ما يجب إعطاؤه؛ إذ ينبغي أن يكون الطفل قد تلقى جميع اللقاحات المستحقة حتى عمره الحالي، وإذا كانت هناك جرعات فائتة فلم يفت الأوان بعد؛ وإعطاء اللقاحات التي يكون الطفل مؤهلاً لها مع مراعاة الفواصل الزمنية اللازمة. الخطوة 3: تذكير مقدّم الرعاية بموعد إحضار الطفل مجدداً لتلقي الجرعات اللاحقة والتأكيد على أهمية استكمال السلسلة. وتزيّن اللوحة رسوم كرتونية لفتاة واقفة ورضيع جالس.
narratives.ru: Панель «Инструкции» из трех шагов для медицинского работника. Шаг 1: похвалить родителя или опекуна за то, что он привел ребенка, и выяснить по карте прививок или со слов опекуна сегодняшний возраст ребенка и уже полученные им вакцины. Шаг 2: использовать таблицу справа, чтобы решить, какие вакцины вводить; ребенок уже должен был получить все вакцины, положенные по его текущему возрасту, а если дозы пропущены — еще не поздно; ввести вакцины, которые показаны ребенку, соблюдая необходимые интервалы. Шаг 3: напомнить опекуну, когда следует снова привести ребенка для получения последующих доз, и подчеркнуть важность завершения серии прививок. Панель украшена мультипликационными рисунками стоящей девочки и сидящего младенца.
narratives.zh: 面向卫生工作者的三步“操作说明”面板。第1步：表扬家长或看护人带儿童前来接种，并通过预防接种证或看护人了解儿童今天的年龄以及已接种过的疫苗。第2步：使用右侧图表决定接种内容；儿童本应已接种截至当前年龄应接种的所有疫苗，如有漏种仍为时不晚；在遵循必要接种间隔的前提下，为儿童接种其符合条件的所有疫苗。第3步：提醒看护人何时带儿童返回接种后续剂次，并强调完成全程接种的重要性。面板配有站立女孩和坐姿婴儿的卡通插图。

narratives.en: A chart titled 'Which vaccines can be given today?', with the line 'It is better to vaccinate late than never!'. Rows are ages (birth, 6 weeks, 10 weeks, 14 weeks, 9 months, 18 months, 2 years); coloured columns are vaccines, each starting at the age of its first dose and running downward as an arrow. HepB BD and BCG start at birth, HepB BD ending at a stop sign; OPV 1-3, PCV 1-3, Penta 1-3 and RV 1-3 at 6, 10 and 14 weeks, RV ending at a stop sign before 2 years; IPV at 14 weeks; MCV 1 at 9 months; DTP4 (or Penta4), MCV 2 and MenA at 18 months. A 'When to give' column gives the timing for each row (for example, at 10 weeks or as soon as possible thereafter, and at least 4 weeks after dose 1), and a 'When not to give' column gives the limits: HepB BD not after 6 weeks; RV1, RV2 and RV3 not after 2 years of age; later doses not before 4 weeks since the previous dose; MCV1 and MenA not before 9 months of age except where indicated. A footer says there is no need to restart a series after a long gap, and there is no upper age limit for most vaccines except rotavirus (under 2 years) and the hepatitis B birth dose (under 6 weeks).
narratives.fr: Tableau intitulé « Quels vaccins peuvent être administrés aujourd'hui ? », accompagné de la mention « Mieux vaut vacciner tard que jamais ! ». Les lignes correspondent aux âges (naissance, 6 semaines, 10 semaines, 14 semaines, 9 mois, 18 mois, 2 ans) ; les colonnes colorées correspondent aux vaccins, chacune débutant à l'âge de sa première dose et descendant sous forme de flèche. Le VHB dose à la naissance (HepB BD) et le BCG commencent à la naissance, HepB BD se terminant par un panneau stop ; les VPO 1–3, PCV 1–3, Penta 1–3 et antirotavirus (RV) 1–3 commencent à 6, 10 et 14 semaines, le RV se terminant par un panneau stop avant 2 ans ; le VPI commence à 14 semaines ; le VAR 1 (MCV 1) à 9 mois ; le DTC4 (ou Penta4), le VAR 2 (MCV 2) et le MenA à 18 mois. Une colonne « Quand administrer » indique le moment prévu pour chaque ligne (par exemple, à 10 semaines ou dès que possible après, et au moins 4 semaines après la dose 1), et une colonne « Quand ne pas administrer » précise les limites : HepB BD pas après 6 semaines ; RV1, RV2 et RV3 pas après l'âge de 2 ans ; les doses suivantes pas moins de 4 semaines après la dose précédente ; MCV1 et MenA pas avant l'âge de 9 mois sauf indication contraire. Un pied de page précise qu'il n'est pas nécessaire de recommencer une série après une longue interruption et qu'il n'y a pas de limite d'âge supérieure pour la plupart des vaccins, à l'exception du rotavirus (moins de 2 ans) et de la dose de vaccin contre l'hépatite B à la naissance (moins de 6 semaines).
narratives.es: Cuadro titulado «¿Qué vacunas pueden administrarse hoy?», con el lema «¡Más vale vacunar tarde que nunca!». Las filas representan las edades (nacimiento, 6 semanas, 10 semanas, 14 semanas, 9 meses, 18 meses, 2 años); las columnas de colores representan las vacunas, cada una comenzando a la edad de su primera dosis y descendiendo en forma de flecha. HepB DN (dosis neonatal) y BCG comienzan al nacer, terminando HepB DN en una señal de alto; OPV 1-3, PCV 1-3, Penta 1-3 y RV 1-3 a las 6, 10 y 14 semanas, terminando RV en una señal de alto antes de los 2 años; IPV a las 14 semanas; MCV 1 a los 9 meses; DTP4 (o Penta4), MCV 2 y MenA a los 18 meses. Una columna «Cuándo administrar» indica el momento para cada fila (por ejemplo, a las 10 semanas o lo antes posible después, y al menos 4 semanas después de la dosis 1), y una columna «Cuándo no administrar» indica los límites: HepB DN no después de las 6 semanas; RV1, RV2 y RV3 no después de los 2 años de edad; las dosis posteriores no antes de que hayan transcurrido 4 semanas desde la dosis previa; MCV1 y MenA no antes de los 9 meses de edad salvo indicación. Una nota al pie señala que no es necesario reiniciar un esquema tras una interrupción prolongada y que no existe límite superior de edad para la mayoría de las vacunas, excepto el rotavirus (menores de 2 años) y la dosis neonatal contra la hepatitis B (menores de 6 semanas).
narratives.ar: مخطط بعنوان «ما اللقاحات التي يمكن إعطاؤها اليوم؟»، مع عبارة «التطعيم المتأخر خير من عدم التطعيم أبداً!». تمثل الصفوف الأعمار (عند الولادة، 6 أسابيع، 10 أسابيع، 14 أسبوعاً، 9 أشهر، 18 شهراً، سنتان)؛ وتمثل الأعمدة الملونة اللقاحات، حيث يبدأ كل عمود عند عمر الجرعة الأولى ويمتد إلى الأسفل على شكل سهم. يبدأ لقاح التهاب الكبد B لحديثي الولادة (HepB BD) ولقاح عصية كالميت غيران (BCG) عند الولادة، وينتهي HepB BD عند علامة توقف؛ وتبدأ لقاحات شلل الأطفال الفموي (OPV 1-3) والمكورات الرئوية المتقارن (PCV 1-3) والخماسي (Penta 1-3) والفيروس العجلي (RV 1-3) عند 6 و10 و14 أسبوعاً، وينتهي RV عند علامة توقف قبل عمر سنتين؛ ويبدأ لقاح شلل الأطفال المعطل (IPV) عند 14 أسبوعاً؛ واللقاح المحتوي على الحصبة (MCV 1) عند 9 أشهر؛ ولقاح DTP4 (أو Penta4) وMCV 2 والمكورات السحائية A (MenA) عند 18 شهراً. ويوضح عمود «متى يُعطى» التوقيت لكل صف (مثلاً عند 10 أسابيع أو في أقرب وقت ممكن بعد ذلك، وبعد 4 أسابيع على الأقل من الجرعة 1)، بينما يوضح عمود «متى لا يُعطى» الحدود: لا يُعطى HepB BD بعد 6 أسابيع؛ ولا تُعطى RV1 وRV2 وRV3 بعد عمر سنتين؛ ولا تُعطى الجرعات اللاحقة قبل مرور 4 أسابيع على الجرعة السابقة؛ ولا يُعطى MCV1 وMenA قبل عمر 9 أشهر إلا حيثما يُشار إلى ذلك. ويذكر تذييل المخطط أنه لا حاجة إلى إعادة بدء السلسلة بعد انقطاع طويل، وأنه لا يوجد حد عمري أقصى لمعظم اللقاحات باستثناء الفيروس العجلي (دون سنتين) وجرعة الولادة من لقاح التهاب الكبد B (دون 6 أسابيع).
narratives.ru: Таблица под названием «Какие вакцины можно ввести сегодня?» с подзаголовком «Лучше привить поздно, чем никогда!». Строки соответствуют возрасту (при рождении, 6 недель, 10 недель, 14 недель, 9 месяцев, 18 месяцев, 2 года); цветные столбцы обозначают вакцины, каждый из которых начинается в возрасте введения первой дозы и идет вниз в виде стрелки. ВГВ при рождении (HepB BD) и БЦЖ (BCG) начинаются при рождении, причем HepB BD заканчивается знаком «стоп»; ОПВ (OPV) 1–3, ПКВ (PCV) 1–3, пентавалентная вакцина (Penta) 1–3 и ротавирусная вакцина (RV) 1–3 — в 6, 10 и 14 недель, при этом RV заканчивается знаком «стоп» до 2 лет; ИПВ (IPV) — в 14 недель; коревая вакцина (MCV 1) — в 9 месяцев; АКДС-4 (DTP4 или Penta4), MCV 2 и MenA — в 18 месяцев. В столбце «Когда вводить» указаны сроки для каждой строки (например, в 10 недель или как можно скорее после этого, и не ранее чем через 4 недели после 1-й дозы), а в столбце «Когда не вводить» приведены ограничения: HepB BD — не позже 6 недель; RV1, RV2 и RV3 — не позже 2-летнего возраста; последующие дозы — не ранее чем через 4 недели после предыдущей дозы; MCV1 и MenA — не ранее 9-месячного возраста, за исключением оговоренных случаев. В примечании внизу указано, что после длительного перерыва начинать серию заново не нужно и что для большинства вакцин верхнего возрастного предела нет, кроме ротавирусной вакцины (до 2 лет) и дозы вакцины против гепатита B при рождении (до 6 недель).
narratives.zh: 标题为“今天可以接种哪些疫苗？”的图表，附有标语“迟种总比不种好！”。各行为年龄（出生、6周、10周、14周、9月龄、18月龄、2岁）；彩色列为疫苗，每列从首剂接种年龄开始并呈箭头向下延伸。乙肝疫苗出生剂次（HepB BD）和卡介苗（BCG）从出生开始，其中HepB BD在停止标志处结束；口服脊灰疫苗（OPV 1-3）、肺炎球菌结合疫苗（PCV 1-3）、五联疫苗（Penta 1-3）和轮状病毒疫苗（RV 1-3）在6、10和14周，其中RV在2岁前的停止标志处结束；灭活脊灰疫苗（IPV）在14周；含麻疹成分疫苗第1剂（MCV 1）在9月龄；百白破第4剂（DTP4或Penta4）、MCV 2和A群流脑疫苗（MenA）在18月龄。“何时接种”列给出各行的时间要求（例如在10周或此后尽早接种，且距第1剂至少4周），“何时不接种”列给出限制条件：HepB BD不超过6周；RV1、RV2和RV3不超过2周岁；后续剂次距前一剂不少于4周；除另有说明外，MCV1和MenA不早于9月龄。页脚注明长时间中断后无需重新开始接种程序，且除轮状病毒疫苗（2岁以下）和乙肝疫苗出生剂次（6周以下）外，大多数疫苗无最大接种年龄限制。

narratives.en: A blank tally sheet for recording vaccinations. Header fields for date, region, district, health facility, location and service delivery strategy (fixed, outreach or mobile). Rows list antigens and items: BCG, Hep B BD, OPV 0-3, IPV, Penta 1-3, Rota 1-3, PCV 1-3, M/MR 1 and 2, DTP4/Other, vitamin A and long-lasting insecticidal net. Each row has rows of tally circles and a total for 0-11 months and for 12 months or older, and a total-vaccinated column. Cells that do not apply are shaded dark: Hep B BD and OPV 0 for 12 months or older, and M/MR 2, DTP4/Other and the net for 0-11 months. A footnote marks Rota 3, DTP4/Other and the net as depending on national health priorities and schedule of services.
narratives.fr: Feuille de pointage vierge pour l'enregistrement des vaccinations. Champs d'en-tête pour la date, la région, le district, l'établissement de santé, le lieu et la stratégie de prestation de services (fixe, avancée ou mobile). Les lignes énumèrent les antigènes et interventions : BCG, Hep B BD, VPO 0–3, VPI, Penta 1–3, Rota 1–3, PCV 1–3, R/RR (M/MR) 1 et 2, DTC4/Autre, vitamine A et moustiquaire imprégnée d'insecticide à longue durée d'action. Chaque ligne comporte des rangées de cercles de pointage et un total pour 0–11 mois et pour 12 mois ou plus, ainsi qu'une colonne du total des vaccinés. Les cellules sans objet sont grisées en foncé : Hep B BD et VPO 0 pour 12 mois ou plus, ainsi que M/MR 2, DTC4/Autre et la moustiquaire pour 0–11 mois. Une note de bas de page indique que Rota 3, DTC4/Autre et la moustiquaire dépendent des priorités sanitaires nationales et du calendrier des services.
narratives.es: Hoja de registro (paloteo) en blanco para anotar las vacunaciones. Campos de encabezado para fecha, región, distrito, establecimiento de salud, localidad y estrategia de prestación del servicio (fija, extramural o móvil). Las filas enumeran los antígenos e insumos: BCG, Hep B DN, OPV 0-3, IPV, Penta 1-3, Rota 1-3, PCV 1-3, SR/S (M/MR) 1 y 2, DTP4/Otra, vitamina A y mosquitero tratado con insecticida de larga duración. Cada fila tiene hileras de círculos de conteo y un total para 0-11 meses y para 12 meses o más, además de una columna de total de vacunados. Las celdas que no corresponden están sombreadas en oscuro: Hep B DN y OPV 0 para 12 meses o más, y M/MR 2, DTP4/Otra y el mosquitero para 0-11 meses. Una nota al pie señala que Rota 3, DTP4/Otra y el mosquitero dependen de las prioridades sanitarias nacionales y del calendario de servicios.
narratives.ar: استمارة تفريغ (حصر) فارغة لتسجيل التطعيمات. تتضمن حقول الترويسة التاريخ والمنطقة والمقاطعة والمرفق الصحي والموقع واستراتيجية تقديم الخدمة (ثابتة أو إيصالية أو متنقلة). وتدرج الصفوف المستضدات والمواد: BCG، وHep B BD، وOPV 0-3، وIPV، وPenta 1-3، وRota 1-3، وPCV 1-3، وM/MR 1 و2، وDTP4/أخرى، وفيتامين أ، والناموسية المعالجة بالمبيدات طويلة الأمد. ويحتوي كل صف على صفوف من دوائر العدّ وإجمالي للفئة العمرية 0–11 شهراً وللفئة 12 شهراً فأكثر، إضافة إلى عمود لإجمالي المطعّمين. وتُظلَّل الخلايا غير المنطبقة بلون داكن: Hep B BD وOPV 0 للفئة 12 شهراً فأكثر، وM/MR 2 وDTP4/أخرى والناموسية للفئة 0–11 شهراً. وتشير حاشية سفلية إلى أن Rota 3 وDTP4/أخرى والناموسية تعتمد على الأولويات الصحية الوطنية وجدول الخدمات.
narratives.ru: Бланк контрольного листка учета прививок. В шапке предусмотрены поля для даты, региона, района, медицинского учреждения, населенного пункта и стратегии предоставления услуг (стационарная, выездная или мобильная). В строках перечислены антигены и профилактические средства: БЦЖ (BCG), ВГВ при рождении (Hep B BD), ОПВ (OPV) 0–3, ИПВ (IPV), пентавалентная вакцина (Penta) 1–3, ротавирусная вакцина (Rota) 1–3, ПКВ (PCV) 1–3, К/КК (M/MR) 1 и 2, АКДС-4/другое (DTP4/Other), витамин A и обработанная инсектицидом длительного действия противомоскитная сетка. Каждая строка содержит ряды кружков для подсчета и итоговое поле для возраста 0–11 месяцев и 12 месяцев и старше, а также столбец общего числа привитых. Неприменимые ячейки закрашены темным цветом: Hep B BD и OPV 0 для возраста 12 месяцев и старше, а также M/MR 2, DTP4/Other и сетка для возраста 0–11 месяцев. В сноске отмечено, что включение Rota 3, DTP4/Other и сетки зависит от национальных приоритетов здравоохранения и графика предоставления услуг.
narratives.zh: 用于记录接种情况的空白划记统计表。表头字段包括日期、地区、县区、卫生机构、地点和服务提供策略（固定、外展或流动）。各行列出抗原及项目：BCG、Hep B BD、OPV 0-3、IPV、Penta 1-3、Rota 1-3、PCV 1-3、麻疹/麻风疫苗（M/MR）1和2、DTP4/其他、维生素A以及长效杀虫剂蚊帐。每行均设有针对0–11月龄和12月龄及以上的划记圆圈行与小计栏，以及总接种人数列。不适用的单元格以深色阴影标示：12月龄及以上的Hep B BD和OPV 0，以及0–11月龄的M/MR 2、DTP4/其他和蚊帐。脚注标明Rota 3、DTP4/其他和蚊帐取决于国家卫生优先事项和服务时间表。

narratives.en: A blank tally sheet for recording vaccinations, the same as the previous one but with three age columns: 0-11 months, 12-23 months and 24 months or older, each with tally circles and a total, and a total-vaccinated column. Rows list BCG, Hep B BD, OPV 0-3, IPV, Penta 1-3, Rota 1-3, PCV 1-3, M/MR 1 and 2, DTP4/Other, vitamin A and long-lasting insecticidal net. Cells that do not apply are shaded dark: Hep B BD and OPV 0 for 12 months and older; Rota 1-3 for 24 months or older; M/MR 2, DTP4/Other and the net for 0-11 months. A footnote marks Rota 3, DTP4/Other and the net as depending on national health priorities and schedule of services.
narratives.fr: Feuille de pointage vierge pour l'enregistrement des vaccinations, identique à la précédente mais comportant trois colonnes d'âge : 0–11 mois, 12–23 mois et 24 mois ou plus, chacune avec des cercles de pointage et un total, ainsi qu'une colonne du total des vaccinés. Les lignes énumèrent BCG, Hep B BD, VPO 0–3, VPI, Penta 1–3, Rota 1–3, PCV 1–3, R/RR (M/MR) 1 et 2, DTC4/Autre, vitamine A et moustiquaire imprégnée d'insecticide à longue durée d'action. Les cellules sans objet sont grisées en foncé : Hep B BD et VPO 0 pour 12 mois et plus ; Rota 1–3 pour 24 mois ou plus ; M/MR 2, DTC4/Autre et la moustiquaire pour 0–11 mois. Une note de bas de page indique que Rota 3, DTC4/Autre et la moustiquaire dépendent des priorités sanitaires nationales et du calendrier des services.
narratives.es: Hoja de registro (paloteo) en blanco para anotar las vacunaciones, igual a la anterior pero con tres columnas de edad: 0-11 meses, 12-23 meses y 24 meses o más, cada una con círculos de conteo y un total, además de una columna de total de vacunados. Las filas enumeran BCG, Hep B DN, OPV 0-3, IPV, Penta 1-3, Rota 1-3, PCV 1-3, SR/S (M/MR) 1 y 2, DTP4/Otra, vitamina A y mosquitero tratado con insecticida de larga duración. Las celdas que no corresponden están sombreadas en oscuro: Hep B DN y OPV 0 para 12 meses y más; Rota 1-3 para 24 meses o más; M/MR 2, DTP4/Otra y el mosquitero para 0-11 meses. Una nota al pie señala que Rota 3, DTP4/Otra y el mosquitero dependen de las prioridades sanitarias nacionales y del calendario de servicios.
narratives.ar: استمارة تفريغ (حصر) فارغة لتسجيل التطعيمات، مطابقة للاستمارة السابقة ولكن بثلاثة أعمدة عمرية: 0–11 شهراً، و12–23 شهراً، و24 شهراً فأكثر، لكل منها دوائر عدّ وإجمالي، بالإضافة إلى عمود لإجمالي المطعّمين. وتدرج الصفوف: BCG، وHep B BD، وOPV 0-3، وIPV، وPenta 1-3، وRota 1-3، وPCV 1-3، وM/MR 1 و2، وDTP4/أخرى، وفيتامين أ، والناموسية المعالجة بالمبيدات طويلة الأمد. وتُظلَّل الخلايا غير المنطبقة بلون داكن: Hep B BD وOPV 0 للفئة 12 شهراً فأكثر؛ وRota 1-3 للفئة 24 شهراً فأكثر؛ وM/MR 2 وDTP4/أخرى والناموسية للفئة 0–11 شهراً. وتشير حاشية سفلية إلى أن Rota 3 وDTP4/أخرى والناموسية تعتمد على الأولويات الصحية الوطنية وجدول الخدمات.
narratives.ru: Бланк контрольного листка учета прививок, аналогичный предыдущему, но с тремя возрастными столбцами: 0–11 месяцев, 12–23 месяца и 24 месяца и старше, каждый с кружками для подсчета и итоговым полем, а также со столбцом общего числа привитых. В строках перечислены БЦЖ (BCG), ВГВ при рождении (Hep B BD), ОПВ (OPV) 0–3, ИПВ (IPV), пентавалентная вакцина (Penta) 1–3, ротавирусная вакцина (Rota) 1–3, ПКВ (PCV) 1–3, К/КК (M/MR) 1 и 2, АКДС-4/другое (DTP4/Other), витамин A и обработанная инсектицидом длительного действия противомоскитная сетка. Неприменимые ячейки закрашены темным цветом: Hep B BD и OPV 0 для возраста 12 месяцев и старше; Rota 1–3 для возраста 24 месяца и старше; M/MR 2, DTP4/Other и сетка для возраста 0–11 месяцев. В сноске отмечено, что включение Rota 3, DTP4/Other и сетки зависит от национальных приоритетов здравоохранения и графика предоставления услуг.
narratives.zh: 用于记录接种情况的空白划记统计表，与前一张相同，但设有三个年龄列：0–11月龄、12–23月龄和24月龄及以上，每列均有划记圆圈和小计栏，并设有总接种人数列。各行列出BCG、Hep B BD、OPV 0-3、IPV、Penta 1-3、Rota 1-3、PCV 1-3、M/MR 1和2、DTP4/其他、维生素A以及长效杀虫剂蚊帐。不适用的单元格以深色阴影标示：12月龄及以上的Hep B BD和OPV 0；24月龄及以上的Rota 1-3；以及0–11月龄的M/MR 2、DTP4/其他和蚊帐。脚注标明Rota 3、DTP4/其他和蚊帐取决于国家卫生优先事项和服务时间表。
